lines: Lap one! The gulls are cheering. I think that is cheering.
A gull just copied my run. Gulls are very good copiers.
If I run past the gull, he has to move. That is the rule.
That gull has been on the fountain for forty-two laps.
I call that gull Captain Wobble. He wobbles.
Do gulls have best friends? I think that one is mine.
Gulls eat chips. I eat chips. We are basically cousins.
A gull looked right at me. I looked back. Nobody blinked.
The cat on the wall is called Madame Moustache. I decided.
The cat on the wall is my referee. She says I won.
Cats can sleep sixteen hours. I tried. I got to four minutes.
The wall cat yawned at me. That means hello in cat.
I did a slow blink at the cat. She did one back! Friends!
Biscuit has four legs, so he is four times faster. Maths.
Biscuit can do a fountain lap in eleven seconds. I counted.
Biscuit sniffed my shoe this morning. It was an honour.
I am saving my crust for Biscuit. It is a very good crust.
When I get a dog I will call him Biscuit Two.
Biscuit wags his tail with his whole back half. Wow.
I am pretending I am Biscuit. Woof! Fast woof!
The gull dance! Arms out, head forward, very serious.
Robot move, then a spin, then a bow. Ta-da!
I practise every afternoon so tonight I am perfect.
My feet know the song before my ears do.
I can spin three times. Four if nobody watches.
This bit goes left, left, jump, wiggle. I invented it.
Papa says my dancing is like popcorn. Popcorn is the best.
I am counting. One, two, three, wiggle. Five, six, wiggle!
When the band plays tonight I will be ready. Very ready.
This is my slow dance. It is slow. Look how slow.
If you jump on the beat, you float for one second. Try it!
I hummed the song from last night. All the way to here.
The dance square has twelve stones across. I measured.
Spin, spin, wobble, stop. The wobble is on purpose.
I am teaching the gull to dance. He is a slow learner.
Henri says I have the feet of a young Fred. Who is Fred?
I can do the moonwalk. Well, the sunwalk. It is daytime.
Dancing practice is like homework, but fun.
Again! Lap twelve. Or lap one of the second go.
I am timing myself. One Mississippi, two Mississ... done!
The fountain is a racetrack and I am the champion.
Clockwise is faster. Anticlockwise is more exciting.
I ran so fast my hat nearly went to Paris.
Lap thirteen. Thirteen is my lucky number since now.
Splash corner! You have to jump there, it is the law.
I race the shadow of the fountain. The shadow cheats.
My shadow is getting longer. That means it is afternoon.
I am a train. Choo! Next stop: the other side of the fountain.
Racing the pigeons. Pigeons do not know they are racing.
I am going to do a hundred laps. Okay, after a snack.
This lap was a world record. The world does not know yet.
Watch! I can run and wave at the same time.
Hopscotch round the fountain. Only the light stones count.
Zigzag lap! Zigzag is twice as long. So twice as good.
I touched the fountain on every side. Four. It is square-ish.
If the fountain was a clock, I would be on half past three.
I found a shell shaped like an ear. Hello, shell!
My pocket has a shell, a pebble and a very good stick.
I am collecting smooth stones. I have seven. Seven is plenty.
I drew a gull in my book. Then I drew him a hat.
My book is about a dragon who runs a bakery. Best book.
I read three pages after lunch. Then a bit of page four.
Henri lets me do one crossword clue. Today I did a whole one!
The clue was 'big cat'. I said Madame Moustache. Henri laughed.
I know a word with seven letters. Fountain. Wait. Eight.
I can whistle now. Sort of. Listen. Fweee.
My kite is at home. It is resting for tomorrow.
I am learning French and Norwegian. Hei! Bonjour! Both!
Odile says I am the tallest I have ever been. True!
The sea is salty so the fish never need to add any. Clever sea.
I can count to a hundred in French. Up to soixante-dix-neuf.
Afternoon is the longest part of the day. I checked.
After my nap I have extra energy. Nap? I did not nap.
I had lunch and now my legs are charged. Like a phone.
The ice cream at the kiosk has a flavour called sunshine.
Lucie rang her bell at me. I rang my pretend bell back.
I waved at Marcel. He bowed. I bowed. Very fancy.
When I am ten I will be ten. That is very soon.
Papa is wandering. Mama is wandering. I am zooming.
There are three kinds of cloud today. Fluffy, fluffy and flat.
If you sit on the warm stones, they hug your legs.
The cypress trees look like green paintbrushes. Swish.
I am going to build a castle out of café sugar cubes.
My best friend runs half a lap behind me. Best friends do that.
Do palm trees get dizzy in the wind? I would.
I can hop on one foot for twenty hops. Other foot, nineteen.
I am thinking of a number. It is big. Bigger. Done.
The fountain sounds like a hundred tiny claps.
There is a cat on the wall and a gull on the lamp. A party.
Madame Moustache has a white sock on one paw. Like me at night.
I danced so much the gull clapped. With his wings. Nearly.
Last lap before snack. Then the first lap after snack.
Lap one! The breeze is pushing me. Thank you, breeze!
I let a pigeon go first. He was in a hurry too.
The fountain splashed me. That was very kind of it.
Running is easier in the afternoon. The air is all warm.
Lap four. My shoes are doing a really good job today.
I am going slow on purpose so Odile can watch properly.
Henri said I run like a swallow. A swallow! Me!
I stopped to say hello to Henri. Laps can wait.
If you wave at me I will wave back. Even mid-lap.
The sun is on my back. It is like a warm hand.
I am doing this lap for Mum. The next one is for Biscuit.
Lap seven is the best lap. It just is.
I found a hair clip on lap three. I gave it to Lucie.
A visitor asked me the way. I ran there with him!
Round and round. The fountain never gets dizzy.
I am counting laps in French now. Un, deux, lots!
Ooh, the spray makes a tiny rainbow if you stand here.
I let my friend win the last one. Do not tell him.
Somebody's hat blew off. I caught it! Very fast catch.
Merci, fountain! Okay, one more. Okay, two more.
The stones are warm from the sun. I can feel it in my shoes.
Henri watered the planter and a bit of me. Thank you!
I am the wind. Whoosh. A nice wind, not a big one.
Every lap I find a new good thing. This lap: a feather.
I gave the feather to Odile. She put it in her hat!
This lap I am running backwards. Carefully. Very carefully.
The ice cream lady waved at me. Two waves, actually.
I say bonjour to everyone on every lap. It is my job.
Do you want to run one lap with me? It is only round.
The palm trees are waving. They are my fans.
I am saving my fastest lap for when Papa comes back.
The fountain sounds like it is laughing. At my jokes, probably.
A gull is racing me from up there. He is cheating, nicely.
I tied my shoelace by myself. Double knot. Like a pro.
Thank you for watching! Most people watch the fountain.
I am pretending the fountain is the sun and I am a planet.
Planet Léo, going round. Very warm planet. Lovely weather.
My friend says I am fast. I say he is fast. We are both fast.
Let me catch my breath. Okay. Got it. Go!
This afternoon smells like lemons and sun cream.
The water is sparkly today. I think it got polished.
Lap twelve, a new record! Last record was also twelve.
I stopped running to tell you your shoes are cool.
Mum said be back by the dancing. I have nineteen minutes.
Henri says hello to the pigeons by name. I am learning them.
That pigeon is Gérard. He is very polite. He nods.
Watch me go round the corner! Whoosh! Did you see?
This is the wave move. The sea taught it to me.
Practising for tonight. Odile is my dance teacher now.
I made up a dance about lemons. It goes like this. Squeeze!
The string lights are not on yet. I am dancing them awake.
This move is called The Biscuit. It has a little hop.
You can dance with me. You do not need to be good. I am not!
Mum says I dance like sunshine. I think that is a yes.
I am practising my bow. Very important. The bow is the end.
The breeze is my partner. It is a good dancer.
Bravo to me! Marcel taught me how to say bravo to me.
I invented a jump. It goes up and then it comes down.
This is for Papa, so he can copy it tonight. Slowly.
One more practice. Then one more. Then it is tonight!
My shadow dances too. It is longer than me. Show-off.
I am the best dancer under ten. I checked. Everyone else is old.
Clap if you like it! Thank you! You can stop now. Or not!
This bit is slow because it is the warm part of the song.
Odile said my twirl was smashing. Smashing is very good.
I do the robot, then the robot gets happy. Like this.
Henri tapped his cane to my dance. That was the drum.
Hands up like palm trees. Now sway. You are a palm tree!
There is no music yet. I am humming it. Badum, badum.
I saved the best move for the end. Wait for it. Wait!
This one is The Fountain. Arms go up and sprinkle down.
I am practising so I can teach my best friend tonight.
Lucie rang her bell when I did my spin. Ding! Applause!
Thank you for being my audience. You are a very good one.
The ground is warm. Good for dancing. Toes like it.
This is the best afternoon. I say that every afternoon.
The breeze smells like the sea and the bakery at once.
I held the door for Odile. She said I am a gentleman. I am!
My hair is all salty and warm. That means summer.
Henri gave me a lemon. I am going to keep it forever.
Thank you, sun, for staying up so long. Very kind.
I helped Marcel carry one spoon. He said it was a big help.
The cicadas are singing. I think they practise too.
I have a plan. Run, then dance, then wave at the sun.
I told the visitor her hat is the best hat in town.
Papa says afternoons are for doing nothing. I do everything.
I gave my friend half my biscuit. The bigger half, nearly.
The shade under the palm is the coolest spot. I am sharing it.
When I sit still I can hear the fountain from here.
Is it still afternoon? Yes! Lots of afternoon left!
Bonjour, madame! Bonjour, monsieur! Bonjour, gull!
Everybody is a bit slower in the afternoon. Except me.
The warm wind just ruffled my hair. Like Papa does.
If you run the other way round, time goes backwards. Maybe.
I am not tired. My legs are just thinking.
Every lap I wave at Henri. He waves back every lap. Twenty waves!
The pigeons are my audience. They are very polite.
Watch my turn at the corner. I call it the Zoom.
When I run past the café it smells like croissants. Bonus speed.
My shoes are the fast ones. The blue ones. They have stripes.
I made up a game. You run and you smile. I am winning.
Tag! You are it. Oh, that was a lamppost. Sorry, lamppost.
The splash bit is where you go extra fast. Science.
If I jump the shadow of the palm, I get a point.
Points so far: forty. Mostly from the palm shadow.
Hide and seek around a fountain is very hard. It is round.
Found you! You were behind the fountain. Again.
Slow lap now. A thinking lap. I am thinking about ice cream.
When I grow up I will run round every fountain in France.
My heart is going boom boom. That means it is happy.
I gave the fountain a high five. It was wet but friendly.
This side is sunny, that side is shady. I like both sides.
Watch me go round without touching the cracks. Nearly!
Marcel said bravo when I ran past. I ran past again for another.
Today the fountain is a castle and I am guarding it. Fast.
I am being a horse now. A very fast seaside horse.
I can run and sing at the same time. Laaa! See?
Running round the fountain makes the whole town spin a bit.
Dizzy! Good dizzy! The cypresses are dancing.
I am collecting smiles. Odile gave me two.
If I splash my hands, that counts as a swim. Mum said.
The fountain has a rainbow at four o'clock. I checked.
Race you to the kiosk! No, wait, back to the fountain!
We are playing ball, but very gently, near the flowers.
Throw it high! Higher than the lamps! Okay, not that high.
Caught it! With two hands and one eye closed.
I lost the ball. Found it. It was hiding under a bench.
Bonjour, fountain. It is me again. Lap fifty, roughly.
I drew a map of the fountain. It is a circle. Very accurate.
This is the starfish. Arms out, legs out, big smile.
My dance has three parts. The middle part is a jump.
I can do the robot and the noodle. Watch the noodle.
Tonight there will be music. I am warming up my elbows.
Mum dances like this. I dance like this. Mine is faster.
This step is called the Croissant. You curl up, then pop!
I practise here because the floor is nice and flat.
When the lamps come on, it is like a party for everyone.
Dancing is like running but you stay in the same place.
I am dancing for the sun so it stays a bit longer.
Papa says my dance is very serious. It is. It is art.
Shoulders up, shoulders down. That is the lamp dance.
Every evening I get better. Tonight I will be amazing.
Wave to the sea, wave to the café, then spin. Ta-da!
Practice makes perfect. I am at practice makes pretty good.
Odile clapped! That means it was a good one.
The lamps are still asleep. They wake up after me.
I can see our window from here. The yellow one with the plant.
Henri's lemons are getting bigger. I check every day.
The sea is very sparkly today. It is showing off.
I love this town. It has a fountain AND a café. Best.
Mum says I have sunshine in my socks. I think she is right.
When the lamps come on, I want to watch the very first one.
I am thinking very hard about a cloud. It looks like a dog.
Today I said bonjour to eleven people. That is a record.
Our window gets the sun at four o'clock. The plant says thanks.
I like when grown-ups sit on benches. It means it is calm time.
The shadows are getting longer. That means more laps first.
My knees are a bit dusty. That means I had a good day.
When I am ten I will be allowed two scoops. I am almost there.
Shh. The fountain is telling a secret. It is just splashing.
Thank you, afternoon. You are very long and very nice.
Soon the windows go yellow, one by one. Like a story.
I am being very quiet now. One second. Okay, that was enough.
Hello! I am Léo. I am nine and three quarters. Nearly ten!
Bonjour, madame! Nice hat! Is it new or just shiny?
Hi Henri! Hi lemon tree! Hi watering can!
Odile! Odile! I did a whole lap without stopping!
Something smells like warm bread. Is it Papa? It is Papa.
Why do gulls shout? Are they telling each other jokes?
The café smells like coffee and also like cake. Mostly cake.
Listen. The fountain goes splish, then splosh. Every time!
Do cypress trees ever want to sit down?
Do lemons know they are sour? Henri says they are proud of it.
The string lights are off. Are they having a nap too?
I can hear a cup clinking. Clink. There, another one!
The palm trees sound like whispering when the wind comes.
Where does the sea go in the afternoon? It is further out!
Bonjour, Marcel! Is today a tarte day or a croissant day?
Who painted all the houses white? They must have had big brushes.
Why are the roofs grey and the walls white? Like a penguin town!
Smell that? Suncream and sea. That is the smell of holidays.
Lucie's bell goes ding. Ding means hello in bicycle.
Mum, can I ask a question? Okay. That was the question. Another!
Is the kiosk man always there? Does he sleep inside the kiosk?
Somebody is playing an accordion. I can do the dance for it!
Wave if you are on holiday! Everyone is waving. Brilliant.
How do bees know which flowers are open? Do the flowers tell them?
I can smell the jasmine on Odile's wall. It smells purple.
Hello, visitor! Welcome to my town. The fountain is that way.
The gulls are louder after lunch. I think they had pudding.
Papa says he is working. He is lying on the bench. Is that work?
Why does the café umbrella go round and round in the wind?
Hello, dog! Not Biscuit. A different dog. Hello anyway!
I counted the cypresses. Twelve. Or the same one twelve times.
Do clouds have names? That one is Bernard.
Ooh, grilled peaches. Somebody is making something very good.
Henri, why do you water the bench? Oh. It was the plant behind.
How tall is the tallest palm? Taller than Papa on Papa.
The stones are warm. My feet say thank you, stones.
Hi Théo! I mean Papa. I said Théo to be funny.
Can I ask you something? What is your favourite ice cream?
When the wind blows, the lights go tinkle tinkle. Listen!
Mmm. Lavender. Odile says it is for calm. I am very calm. Watch.
Does the sea ever stop? Even on Sundays?
I said hello to the gull. He did not say it back. Shy gull.
I love the sound of Marcel's tray. Tink tink tink. Coming through!
Why do grown-ups sit so much? Is sitting a grown-up sport?
Good afternoon, everybody! That is a very polite thing to shout.
What does the promenade sound like at night? Mum says quiet.
Hi, Henri! Bye, Henri! Hi again, Henri!
Who wants to race? You? You? Fine, I will race my shadow.
Lap six. My shoes squeak on lap six. Squeak lap!
I am going to run so fast my hair stays behind.
Can you hear my feet? Pat pat pat pat. That is speed.
Excuse me! Fast person coming! Thank you! Merci!
The fountain is the middle of the world. I checked.
This lap I am a cheetah. Next lap I am a very fast snail.
I smell crêpes on this side and roses on that side. Best lap.
Hello again, lady with the sunhat! That was lap four hellos.
I am running backwards now. Very carefully. Very slowly.
The water sounds different on this side. Bubblier.
Can a person run forever? I will try until snack time.
My new record is fast. I do not know how fast. Very.
Hello, Lucie! Your bike is faster but I have more legs. Two!
Round and round and round! I could do this till I am ten.
Is it a lap if I stop to look at the fish? Half a lap.
This is the spinny bit. Hold on to your hat!
Can you hear the music? It is in my head. It is very good.
One, two, jump! One, two, bigger jump!
Do grown-ups practise dancing? Papa says he is a natural.
This is the gull dance. Flap, flap, look for crisps.
Mum, will they play the accordion song tonight? The twirly one?
I am saving my best move for tonight. This is my second best.
Shall we dance, madame? It is okay, I can lead.
The ground is hot so I am dancing on my tiptoes. Ballet!
Clap, clap, stomp. That is the whole song. I made it up.
Do fish dance? Paul wiggles. I think wiggling counts.
I heard music from a window. Now I am dancing to the window.
Hello, people! Do you want to see a jump? Here is a jump!
Tonight the lights come on and everyone dances. Even Henri!
Dancing smells like sunshine. I do not know why. It just does.
The promenade is two hundred and twelve of my steps. I checked.
I am writing Mamie a postcard. It says FOUNTAIN in big letters.
Papi lives in Paris. His roofs are grey like ours. Twins!
Mamie in Provence has a lavender field. A whole field. Purple!
Guess what. I can tie my shoes in four seconds now.
I lost a tooth this morning! Number six. Six is a lot.
Norway has a sun that stays up all night. Asgeir told me.
When I go to Paris I will climb the tower. Every step.
My postcard to Papi has a palm tree and a cypress. Both!
The promenade goes kiosk, café, fountain, lamps, sea. In order.
Mamie sends lavender in her letters. Our letterbox smells lovely.
I got a gold star for spelling. Spelling is easy. Mostly.
I know the way to the kiosk with my eyes closed. Nearly.
Papi says Paris has a hundred bakeries. Papa would faint.
I walked the whole promenade backwards. Only bumped one bench.
Every lamp on the promenade has a number. Mine is seven.
Mamie's letter came today! She drew a cat. A good cat.
I am nine and three quarters. Soon nine and four quarters.
The kiosk man knows my name now. Officially a regular.
In Provence the crickets sing all day. Here the gulls do.
Next summer we go to Mamie's. I am packing already. Socks.
I can count to twenty in Norwegian. En, to, tre... lots!
The promenade has three cats. I named them all Paul.
A postcard with a stamp goes all the way to Paris. Brave card.
Papi sent a photo of a pigeon. Paris pigeons look fancy.
I found a perfect round stone. It is going in a postcard.
My route: home, fountain, bench, café, railing. Then again!
If I walk on only the white tiles I get a superpower.
My friend and I made a map of the promenade. It has dragons.
Asgeir is from Norway. That is the snow one. And fjords!
Mamie says the Provence sun is the same sun as ours. Sharing!
I beat my own record. Bench to fountain in nineteen seconds.
The promenade is longest in the afternoon. Shadows add bits.
I am going to write to Papi every single day. Or Sundays.
I learned a new word: magnifique. It means really good.
In Norway they eat brown cheese. Brown! Like a biscuit.
I swept the step for Mum. She gave me a medal. A biscuit medal.
If you stand on the bench you can see all the roofs. Zinc!
Paris is so far you need a whole train. A long one.
Henri let me water one lemon tree. It said thank you. I think.
Mamie is coming to visit! In eleven sleeps. Ten and a half.
I drew the whole promenade for Papi. The sea is extra blue.
I have walked the promenade a thousand times. Maybe forty.
My best route has a cypress at the end. For shade and luck.
I can do a cartwheel! Small one. Medium-small.
My letter to Mamie is two pages. One is a drawing of Biscuit.
When it is afternoon here it is also afternoon in Paris. Same!
Papa says in Norway the lakes go hard and you can walk on them.
I have a stamp from Provence. It has a lemon on it. Henri's?
I counted the palm trees on the promenade. Nine. Like me!
Mum says I was very good today. I was very very good.
Marcel let me carry one glass. Didn't spill. Not one drop.
The gulls go the same route as me. We are a team.
Papi says the Seine is a river that goes round Paris. Twisty.
I am saving postcards. I have fourteen. Fifteen with this one.
In Provence Mamie has a blue door. We have a blue door too!
Round the fountain and back! Personal best! I think!
This lap is for Mamie. She is watching from Provence. Kind of.
Ready, steady... wait, my shoelace. Okay. Go!
This lap I am Paris. Next lap I am Norway. Very cold lap.
Lap fifteen! New record! Somebody write it down!
I am the promenade postman. Delivering laps!
I jumped over the puddle by the fountain. Easy. Long legs.
This is my lucky lap. I can feel it in my socks.
Henri timed me with his watch. He said splendid!
Two more laps and then a postcard break. Maybe three.
Tag! You are it! No take-backs! The fountain is base!
This is the Paris dance. You do it with a fancy nose.
This move is called the Provence. You wiggle like lavender.
I made up a Norway dance. It is very cold. Brrr. Brrr. Jump!
Watch my spin! One and a half spins! New record!
I learned this step from Papi. He learned it in Paris.
This is the postcard dance. Stamp! Stamp! Send!
Mum says I dance like Papa. Papa says I dance better.
Tonight I will dance with Mum. I have practised the bow.
This one is the promenade shuffle. Bench, bench, fountain!
I did the big jump and landed it. Big achievement.
Mamie said send her a dance. I will draw it on a postcard.
This is my bread dance for Papa. You are the baguette.
I am learning to skip with a rope. Twenty skips! Then a tangle.
Look, a handstand! Two seconds! The sky was at the bottom.
I can juggle two lemons. Three lemons is next summer.
Henri is teaching me boules. You throw it gently, like a secret.
My boule landed right by the little one. Henri said ooh la la.
I am practising my wheelbarrow walk. I just need a Papa for it.
Learning to balance on the low wall. Arms out like a gull.
I can stand on one leg like a flamingo. For ages. Count!
I learned to throw a paper aeroplane. It flew to the kiosk!
I folded a paper frog. Press his back and he jumps. Boing!
Leapfrog over the bollards! Only the short ones. Safety.
Running quietly, like a cat. Shh. Pat. Pat.
Every afternoon I practise my starts. Crouch, look, ZOOM.
My very first lap was round this fountain. Mum held my hand.
I practise my big jump over the drain. Today: cleared it!
My left foot is learning to kick. Lefty is a bit shy.
Hoop rolling! You tap it and it goes. Odile had one too.
Bounce, step, bounce, step. I can walk and bounce a ball now!
Wheee! I learned to spin on one heel. Lucie showed me.
I can skip backwards now. Forwards is for beginners. Joke!
Egg and spoon race, but with a lemon. Gold medal to me.
Remember the summer race on the promenade? I came third. Of ten!
Statues! Everybody freeze! Henri is brilliant at statues.
Catching with one hand! The other hand does the waving.
Ball against the wall: ten catches. Odile counted out loud.
Diabolo! It goes up off the string and comes down. Mostly.
Yo-yo practice. Down is easy. Up is still learning.
Leap, land, bow. That is how a champion finishes.
Hula hoop! It stays up if you wiggle like you mean it.
Roller skates today! The promenade is very smooth.
Kerb balancing, ten steps! Papa says I am a tightrope man.
Waltzing is like walking in a triangle. I am getting it!
I learned the cha-cha from the radio. Cha-cha-cha. Cha!
Practising the twist. Like drying your back with a towel!
My tap dancing has no tap shoes. I say tap with my mouth.
I am learning to clap on the off beat. It is the tricky beat.
Last summer I danced with Odile at the fête. She let me lead!
I remember the first night the string lights came on. Magic!
Dancers look at one spot when they spin. My spot is the kiosk.
Tiptoes, heels, tiptoes, heels. Odile says that is ballet.
Tonight I lead the farandole. I am practising the front bit.
My arms are doing the swan. My legs are doing the duck.
I learned to snap my fingers! Snap. Okay, it is a quiet snap.
Mum showed me her dance from when she was nine. Very bouncy.
I am making a dance with a beginning, a middle and a bow.
Learning the splits. I am at the halfway splits so far.
Practising the jive. Kick, kick, step, step. Phew!
When I was six I danced in Papa's shoes. Huge shoes. Best dance.
Last summer the accordion played and I danced till dark.
This dance spells my name. L is an arm, E is a leg, O is a spin.
I am learning my seven times table. Seven, fourteen, lots.
Seven times eight is fifty-six. I practised it on the stairs.
Henri taught me the church clock. It says ten past four!
I am learning a poem by heart. It is about a crow and a fox.
I learned to wink! Watch. Both eyes. Okay, one is practising.
Joined-up writing! My L has a loop now. Fancy L.
I practised my signature. It is a big Léo and a star.
That pink one is bougainvillea. I learned it today. Big word!
Marcel is teaching me to fold napkins. This one is a fan.
I learned which way is north. The sea is the other way.
Tongue twister: six slim swans. Six swim slans. Nearly!
Papa taught me a riddle. What has hands but cannot clap? A clock!
My sunflower grew a whole centimetre. I measured with my finger.
Henri showed me how lemons start. A flower first! Then a lemon.
I am learning the stars for tonight. The Big Dipper goes first.
Learning to draw hands. Mine have six fingers. Still practising.
I am learning the recorder. It squeaks. Mum says that is music.
I squeezed my first lemon all by myself. My hands smell yellow.
